newsitem.title: MAURITIUS: Mauritian bourse sets targets to June 1997.
newsitem.headline: Mauritian bourse sets targets to June 1997.

text.p: The Stock Exchange of Mauritius will modernise rules, restructure its administration, launch an electronic trading system and launch new instruments to tap foreign investment in the year to June, 1997, an official said.
The official told Reuters on Thursday a Central Depository System for electronic share settlement will be in place in mid December and was seen as a boost to investor participation.
The official saw the new trading system as a forerunner to electronic trading in the Indian Ocean island.

Other longer term development avenues listed by the bourse include developing a bond market, continuous training of share dealers, stockbrokers, fund managers and the study of regional cooperation with other bourses in neighbouring countries.

The Stock Exchange of Mauritius will also be restructured into four departments, Trading & Market Information, Marketing & Development, Legal Affairs, Finance & Administration, each under the responsibility of a manager, the official said.
"The new structure gives the expertise and organisational depth which will allow it to ensure its long term development as well as that of the Mauritian market," the official said.
"During the year 1996/97, the bourse intends to review and modernise its rules as a whole," the official told Reuters.
In July, Stock Exchange of Mauritius chief executive Richard Morin said current rules were "lacking in terms of international standards". He gave no details at the time.
Bourse officials said the bourse would step up an information and marketing campaign to attract more individual, institutional and foreign investors.
They said initiatives would include courses on the potential role of the bourse in savings of individuals to setting up of a data base for use by foreign investors interested in investing.
The marketing campaign will also target local institutional investors whose participation is seen low in the market.
The Stock Exchange of Mauritius has 42 listed companies with a total market capitalisation of 30.2 billion rupees ($1.4 billion). It trades on Mondays, Wednesdays and Fridays.
